findings.description: AC-9 still cannot pass against the current docs. The only skip reasons allowed are 'a call to a method of a later wave (named)' or 'an illustrative copy of an existing type declaration (such as Method or RouteHandler)'. Several blocks fit neither reason and cannot compile with the wave 3 main classes: (a) docs/api/json.md block 1 `public class User { @SerializedName("id") private String id; ...}` needs Gson, which is not on the NaruServe-api classpath; (b) docs/api/lifecycle.md block 1 `public interface ApplicationContext extends ServiceRegistry { ... Logger logger(); }` refers to `Logger`, which no wave 3 class or block in that file declares; (c) docs/api/json.md `public interface JsonCodec { <T> T decode(Reader reader, Type type) throws IOException; ...}`, multipart.md `UploadFile` (InputStream, File, OutputStream) and middleware.md `Middleware`/`Next` (Request, Response) compile 'as its own compilation unit' only if the test adds imports, and the AC does not say it does. Middleware, Next, JsonCodec, UploadFile, Logger, ServiceRegistry and ApplicationContext are declarations of later-wave types, not 'copies of an existing type', so none of them can go on the skip list.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the skip reasons to cover 'declares or uses a type that a later wave or a third-party module (Gson) provides (named)', matching the docs-examples decision that a later-wave example joins the compiled set in its own wave. Also state that type-declaration units and the method template get fixed imports (java.io.*, java.lang.reflect.Type, java.util.*, com.snoworca.naruserve.*).

findings.ac: Requirement statement vs AC-9; Verification Method
findings.description: The requirement statement is only about markers: 'record the wave 3 decisions in docs/api/request.md, response.md, routing.md, app.md, defaults.md and express-migration.md, removing the (미확정) markers ...'. AC-9 adds a different obligation that the statement does not hold: compile every ```java block of every docs/api/*.md (I-009), which covers files outside the six (json.md, lifecycle.md, middleware.md, multipart.md, logging.md, sse.md, static.md), plus relabelling fences. The Verification Method is 'inspection', but AC-9 is an automated root-suite test. The trace links name only the six files and RoutingDocsTest, not the docs-compile test.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the statement with 'and keep every docs/api Java example whose methods exist at the wave 3 merge compiling (I-009)', set Verification Method to test (or inspection+test), and add a trace row for the docs-compile test. Or move AC-9 into its own OPS requirement for I-009.

findings.description: AC-7 replaces only 'the express.raw()/express.text() marker' (express-migration.md:84 `| express.raw(), express.text() | **(미확정)** |`). The same file also lists the feature as undecided at :296-300 ('다음은 사양서에 없어서 **(미확정)** 입니다 ... - 원본 본문 읽기(express.raw(), express.text())'). AC-7 and AC-8 do not say whether that bullet goes. If it stays, the file says both that v1 has no raw or text reader and that the question is undecided, which breaks the body-ownership decision ('Wave 3 replaces the express.raw()/express.text() marker ... with the statement that v1 has no raw or text body reader').
findings.suggested_fix: Have AC-7 also remove the raw/text bullet from the undecided list at express-migration.md §'Express에 있지만 아직 정해지지 않은 기능', or move it under a 'not in v1' statement.

findings.description: This is not a contradiction. FR-HTTP-014 AC-7 makes the copy run after the handler returns, so the condition in FR-HTTP-016 AC-4, 'when the handler returns before the copy ends', is always true. 'During res.stream(...) the response is STREAMING' reads as 'during the call', but under AC-7 the call only commits and returns. The two ACs agree in substance; only the wording is loose.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword as: 'After res.stream(...) returns, the response is STREAMING until the copy ends, then COMPLETED, or ABORTED on abort.'

findings.description: The branch 'throws after commit while the response is COMMITTED' cannot be reached from a wave 3 handler. send, html, send(byte[]) and end go from COMMITTED to COMPLETED within one call (FR-HTTP-016 AC-1), and stream() leaves the response STREAMING (FR-HTTP-016 AC-4). Only the STREAMING and COMPLETED branches can be tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop 'COMMITTED or' from AC-3, or say the COMMITTED case is checked with an internal DefaultResponse unit test.

findings.description: AC-2 says 'a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET abc` and `GET /%2e%2e` are answered 400'. `abc` is rejected by the separate non-'/' rule (FR-HTTP-005 AC-3), not by the PathValidator, so it does not show the validator ordering it is cited for.
findings.suggested_fix: Use only validator cases (e.g. `/%2e%2e`, `/a%2Fb`) for the validator ordering and cite `abc` under the non-'/' rule.

findings.description: AC-6 tags '[wave decision: Working app in wave 3]', but that decision says nothing about how a real upgrade request to a WebSocket route is answered before wave 7. The 426 answer to a client that already offered `Upgrade: websocket` is an SRS-level choice, allowed under C-07, but the tag attributes it to a decision that does not contain it.
findings.suggested_fix: Tag it as an implementer decision under C-07 (or the wave-7 deferral), not as the 'Working app' decision.

findings.description: D-105 says the SPI gives the core 'the request line'. AC-1 splits this into the method token, raw path and raw query, and the HTTP version of the request line is missing. No AC states whether the version crosses the SPI.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the protocol version to AC-1, or state that the adapter alone handles the version.

findings.description: The automatic-response-bodies decision says 'Wave 3 tests assert status and headers only'. These ACs also assert 'an empty body'. This is consistent with `Content-Length: 0`, but it ties the tests to a body that wave 4 replaces.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert `Content-Length: 0` (a header) and drop the separate empty-body assertion, or note that wave 4 restates these ACs.

summary.coverage: All 55 design items (D-040..D-046, D-071..D-109, D-392..D-399, D-442) are cited. Every wave decision, the carried bullets, loop-D V1-006/V2-004 and the three residual bullets have ACs with the decided values (rawPath without query, application/octet-stream, stream closes, ClassCastException, app.routerPolicy, HEAD, empty-body 4xx/5xx, ISE after freeze, null removes, 426 TinyHttpd deferred).
summary.checked_no_issue: FR-HTTP-016 AC-4 vs FR-HTTP-014 AC-7 agree (wording only, F3-04). The values match the code: Allow order and contents (Router.allowOf, MethodSet declaration order), Method.any() without TRACE/CONNECT, Router.lookup throwing on a validator-rejected path (so validation must come first), addWebSocket and the MATCHED/WEBSOCKET upgrade result, RouterPolicy builder names, @NullMarked packages. The routing.md marker set left after removal is exactly one line (use(middleware)), consistent with OPS-ROUTE-002 AC-3. The request.md jsonTree()/jsonMap() marker exists (AC-8 is not fabricated). No AC requires a D-392 later-wave method or a deferred TinyHttpd half. No wave 1/2 test regression found other than the intended RoutingDocsTest change. BuildLayoutTest only rejects module/coordinate markers.
